title: Working with the seed table
text: Create columns (names can changed cols argument octo_update_ids()): Keep ID columns Text. IDs 64-bit integers, Number columns silently change last digits. Positions can pasted straight Neuroglancer: 1234, 5678, 910, [1234 5678 910] tab-separated values work.

title: Working with the seed table
text: first run looks supervoxel every seed, roughly 0.3 1 second per point. Later runs look new seeds refresh root IDs, takes seconds. Running daily (cron job scheduled task) keeps table current.
code: library(octor) octo_update_ids(dry_run = TRUE)   # see what would change octo_update_ids()                 # write to SeaTable

title: Working with the seed table
text: several rows point root ID, neuron. group, one row primary row, one annotate; others secondary: tick primary row want keep row ticked, octor picks row annotation filled (cell_type, group, soma_side, reconstructor, annotator, seymour_match_id), oldest row equal CONFLICT means several rows ticked. usually happens proofreading merged two neurons annotated: merge information one row untick merged neuron split , rows become unique Useful SeaTable views: Duplicates: filter n_seeds > 1, group root_id annotate: filter dup_status secondary: one row per neuron

title: Working with the seed table
code: ids <- octo_find_ids("^MBON")                     # regex on cell_type ids <- octo_find_ids("KC", exact = TRUE)          # exactly "KC" ids <- octo_find_ids("^L$", column = "soma_side") seeds <- octo_seeds(trusted_only = TRUE)          # whole table, one row per neuron

title: Working with the seed table
text: Meshes downloaded parallel kept memory R session, plotting neurons instant.
code: nl <- octo_read_meshes(ids)          # 10% of faces, fast to plot nl[, c("cell_type", "soma_side")] rgl::plot3d(nl)  nl_full <- octo_read_meshes(ids, simplify = 1)   # full resolution

title: Seymour and octo
text: registration file (seymour_octo_reg.rds, 60 MB) shared separately. Point octor , e.g. ~/.Rprofile: : seymour2octo() octo2seymour() work neurons, neuronlists, meshes point matrices. coordinates nm. Spelunker shows octo 8 nm voxels; convert octo_nm2voxel() octo_voxel2nm().
code: options(octor.seymour_reg = "/path/to/seymour_octo_reg.rds") library(octor) library(catmaid) conn <- catmaid_login(server = "...", token = "...")  nl <- read_seymour_neurons("annotation:^MBON$", conn = conn) nl_octo <- seymour2octo(nl)            # skeletons and connectors  meshes <- octo_read_meshes(octo_find_ids("^MBON")) rgl::plot3d(meshes, alpha = 0.3) rgl::plot3d(nl_octo, col = "red")

title: Seymour and octo
text: Landmarks: 30 corresponding points (midline points every VNC segment mushroom body landmarks sides) give affine transform. Octo 1.4 times larger Seymour x y 1.2 times z; mirroring. Synapse clouds: smooth non-rigid warp pulls Seymour’s presynaptic connectors onto octo’s synapse predictions (synapses_v8), coarse fine, landmarks kept place. Errors measured 5-fold cross-validation landmarks. weakest region posterior VNC. Seymour’s connectors sparse, landmarks midline. Adding lateral landmarks brain outside mushroom body easiest way improve .

title: Seymour and octo
text: landmark sheet needs columns include, seymour_loc octo_loc (nm, "x, y, z"). rows include set TRUE used.
code: lm  <- read_seymour_octo_landmarks("seymour_octo_reg.csv") syn <- octo_synapse_positions()                       # resumable download con <- seymour_connectors("annotation:^all_somas$", conn = conn)  reg <- fit_seymour_octo_reg(   lm,   syn[, c("pre_pt_position_x", "pre_pt_position_y", "pre_pt_position_z")],   con[, c("x", "y", "z")],   cv_folds = 5) reg saveRDS(reg, "seymour_octo_reg.rds")

what: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: R tools octo L1 larva connectome CAVE (zlatic_octo-2_datastack), SeaTable table neuron seeds, Seymour L1 larva CATMAID. keep supervoxel root IDs SeaTable current, flag neurons seeded find neurons cell type read meshes (simplified fast plotting) query synapses, download synapse positions transform neurons Seymour octo (landmarks + synapse-cloud registration)

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: octor lives private repository. install need read access (ask repository owner add collaborator) GitHub token: Use classic token. Fine-grained tokens often read private repositories owned another account.
code: install.packages(c("remotes", "usethis", "gitcreds")) usethis::create_github_token()   # tick the "repo" scope, generate, copy the token gitcreds::gitcreds_set()         # paste the token when asked remotes::install_github("eichlerkathi/octor")

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: octor talks CAVE, SeaTable CloudVolume Python (via reticulate). Install Python packages : natverse package fafbseg installed, uses fafbseg::simple_python(), octor shares natverse Python environment. Otherwise octor creates environment prints RETICULATE_PYTHON=... line add ~/.Renviron. Restart R afterwards.
code: octor::octo_python_setup()

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: opens token page octo CAVE server browser. Log , copy token paste R console. octor checks token works saves CAVE_TOKEN_BRAININBRAIN ~/.Renviron, . Tokens CAVE datasets affected. token yet, use octo_get_token(new = TRUE).
code: library(octor) octo_get_token()

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: SeaTable, open base, ? menu ? Advanced ? API Token create token read-write permission. Add ~/.Renviron (open file usethis::edit_r_environ()): Restart R.
code: SEATABLE_API_TOKEN=<API token of the SeaTable base>

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
code: library(octor) octo_python_check()   # Python and packages octo_find_ids("KC")   # SeaTable connection

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: R uses wrong Python: reticulate picks Python per session. Set RETICULATE_PYTHON=/path//python ~/.Renviron restart R. Mesh synapse results look like Python objects instead R data: update reticulate (install.packages("reticulate")); numpy 2 needs reticulate 1.38 newer. Token rejected: run octo_get_token() ; tokens can expire.

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: Defaults set R options. change one, e.g. ~/.Rprofile: See ?octor options.
code: options(octor.seatable_table = "Seeds",         octor.seatable_url   = "https://cloud.seatable.io",         octor.seymour_reg    = "~/data/seymour_octo_reg.rds")

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: seed table needs columns: position (Text, Spelunker voxel coordinates), supervoxel_id, root_id, root_id_previous, dup_status same_as (Text), root_changed_on ids_checked_on (Date), n_seeds (Number) primary (Checkbox). Keep ID columns Text: Number columns corrupt 64-bit IDs. Neurons several seeds share root ID. group, tick primary row trust. row ticked, row annotation filled picked. SeaTable view filtered n_seeds > 1 grouped root_id shows groups together.
code: octo_update_ids()                 # supervoxels, root IDs, double-seed flags seeds <- octo_seeds(trusted_only = TRUE)

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
code: ids <- octo_find_ids("^MBON")             # regex on cell_type nl  <- octo_read_meshes(ids)              # 10% of faces by default nl[, c("cell_type", "soma_side")] rgl::plot3d(nl)

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
code: syn <- octo_synapses(pre = ids)           # needs a materialized datastack pos <- octo_synapse_positions()           # all positions, no root IDs, resumable

title: Tools for the Octo L1 Larva Connectome
text: registration file (60 MB) package. Get : https://drive.google.com/file/d/1NJ-pJxH3CVPlpYD6es03B_MLNaUVh44h/view?usp=sharing, point options(octor.seymour_reg = ...) (file path URL), fit : current 30 landmarks, cross-validated error 3.6 µm.
code: library(catmaid) conn <- catmaid_login(server = ..., token = ...) nl <- read_seymour_neurons("annotation:^MBON$", conn = conn) nl_octo <- seymour2octo(nl)               # skeletons + connectors, nm lm  <- read_seymour_octo_landmarks("seymour_octo_reg.csv") con <- seymour_connectors("annotation:^all_somas$", conn = conn) reg <- fit_seymour_octo_reg(lm, pos[, c("pre_pt_position_x", "pre_pt_position_y",                                         "pre_pt_position_z")],                             con[, c("x", "y", "z")], cv_folds = 5) saveRDS(reg, "seymour_octo_reg.rds")

what: Fit a Seymour -> octo registration — fit_seymour_octo_reg
title: Fit a Seymour -> octo registration — fit_seymour_octo_reg
text: Affine fit landmarks, coarse--fine non-rigid warp pulls Seymour synapse cloud onto octo synapse cloud keeping landmarks place.

title: Fit a Seymour -> octo registration — fit_seymour_octo_reg
code: fit_seymour_octo_reg(   landmarks,   octo_xyz,   seymour_xyz,   holdout = NULL,   cell = 2000,   sigma = c(24000, 12000, 6000, 3000),   iter = c(6, 6, 5, 4),   trim = c(12000, 8000, 5000, 3000),   landmark_weight = 1000,   regularise = 5,   cv_folds = 0 )

title: Fit a Seymour -> octo registration — fit_seymour_octo_reg
text: landmarks output read_seymour_octo_landmarks() octo_xyz octo synapse positions (n x 3, nm), e.g. presynaptic positions octo_synapse_positions() seymour_xyz Seymour connector positions (n x 3, nm), e.g. seymour_connectors() holdout landmark rows used fitting, measure error cell downsampling grid (nm) sigma, iter, trim smoothing width (nm), iterations maximum matching distance (nm) per level landmark_weight many cloud points landmark counts regularise pulls warp towards zero points cv_folds > 0, also estimate error k-fold cross-validation landmarks (takes cv_folds times longer)

title: Fit a Seymour -> octo registration — fit_seymour_octo_reg
text: seymour_octo_reg object; save saveRDS()
